clue.text: All possible orders of prime numbers

indicators.note: the answer is a piece of the two words that follow, so they are what it is made of

explanation.surface: A mathematician lists every possible ordering of a set of prime numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orders' looks like the mathematical word for arrangements, but it means what diners ask for; the letters straddle 'priME NUmbers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's bill of fare lists every dish a diner can ask the kitchen for.

clue.text: Boatman's helm is prime mover about tacking east at first

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each word from the possessive ending through to the final word is used

explanation.surface: The setter's helmsman steers, turning round and tacking east.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter's own name; the S comes from the possessive ending of 'Boatman's', then the initials of 'helm is prime mover about tacking east'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow sailor on the same vessel, so a companion to someone who works boats.

clue.text: Spring and Fall

definitions.meaning: a spring is a light skipping step, as in tripping along
to stumble over something and fall

explanation.surface: Two seasons, spring and autumn (the American fall).
explanation.walkthrough: The seasons are a false trail: both words are verbs of movement on the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a light nimble step and a stumble that sends someone down.

clue.text: Wrap leading edge (add less if turbulent)

indicators.note: the letters of the bracketed word are subtracted from the longer phrase
turbulent air is churned about, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aeronautical note about a wing's leading edge and turbulence.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A, D, D away from LEADINGEDGE to leave LEINGEGE, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A flimsy dressing gown worn by women is a light garment wrapped around the body.

clue.text: Prime impeachment

definitions.meaning: to prime a gun is to load it with powder
a formal accusation against an official

explanation.surface: A first-class impeachment, as a headline adjective and noun.
explanation.walkthrough: In a puzzle full of prime numbers, 'Prime' here is a verb about loading a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To load a firearm is to fill it with powder, and an indictment accuses someone formally.

clue.text: Trump's usual response to criticism, Donald's leadership heading off trouble twice as stock index falls one point

indicators.note: the leading letter of the name is taken
the head of the next word is removed
the beheading happens two times, so two opening letters go

parts.note: the Dow Jones index on Wall Street
N, north, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: A political jibe at how the President meets criticism while markets slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off ... twice' strips T then R from 'trouble', leaving OUBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To redouble a commitment when challenged, a phrase from blackjack for staking more.

clue.text: Limited by metal casing in computers etc

indicators.note: the metal forms a case round the other pieces

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
IT, information technology

explanation.surface: Computers limited by being housed in metal cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with bounds or an end is restricted in extent.

clue.text: Perhaps a prime, cut from cube efficiently

indicators.note: the letters are sliced out of the middle of the following words

explanation.surface: A butcher cuts a prime joint from a cube of meat efficiently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' is no number here but top-quality meat; the letters sit inside 'cuBE Efficiently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime is a grade of top-quality meat, and steak from cattle is an example.

clue.text: Number one from one of two

indicators.note: one taken from the longer word means that letter is removed

parts.note: either means one or the other of two
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Choosing number one from a pair of options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but something that numbs, an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that numbs, an old anaesthetic gas used in surgery.

clue.text: He noticed creeping destruction of cultural identity

indicators.note: the letters creep about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spots a slow, creeping erosion of a people's culture.
explanation.definitionFit: The deliberate wiping out of an ethnic group's culture rather than its people.

clue.text: Rejected wordplay quietly sent back by Paul or edited

indicators.note: the quiet letter is moved to the back of the word

parts.note: a pun is play on words
p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly

indicators.note: the words are edited into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An editor dislikes Paul's puns and sends them back.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving P to the back of PUN gives UNP; 'edited' rearranges PAULOR into OPULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Disliked and turned down by people at large, so out of favour.

clue.text: Transient prime

definitions.meaning: to prime someone is to instruct them in advance

explanation.surface: A short-lived prime, as an adjective and a noun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime' is a verb here: to give someone instructions before a task.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting a short time, and to give instructions to someone before a mission.

clue.text: Prime suspect in deal with Government

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective, dubious, so the letters are unsound and rearranged

explanation.surface: The chief suspect was in a deal with the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime suspect' reads as a phrase, but 'Prime' is the definition and 'suspect' rearranges INDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime as an adjective means foremost, chief or principal.

clue.text: Enjoy yourself! I've gone out to get drunk

indicators.note: the letters of the contraction have left the phrase

parts.note: to live it up is to have a riotous good time

explanation.surface: A party-goer urged to enjoy themselves has gone out to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking IVE from LIVEITUP leaves L, IT, UP.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal adjective for intoxicated, as if glowing with alcohol.

clue.text: Be alive in time to be reborn for certain

indicators.note: being reborn gives the letters a new form

explanation.surface: A believer in reincarnation is sure of coming back to life in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bound to happen is sure, beyond doubt.

clue.text: Perhaps fire English workers allowed outside

indicators.note: the permitted word goes outside the workers

parts.note: let means allowed
men can mean workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: An English workforce is allowed to work outside, perhaps to fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Fire was one of the four classical elements, with earth, air and water.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire is one of the four classical elements of the ancient world, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Prime every other T-shirt, even

indicators.note: taking alternate letters, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A prime T-shirt in every other drawer, even.
explanation.definitionFit: Divisible only by itself and one, so a prime number.

clue.text: Boatman finishes article on primes

indicators.note: the setter's pronoun comes at the end, after the article

parts.note: the definite article
Boatman is the setter, so he is me

explanation.surface: The setter completes an article about prime numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym; the puzzle's subject is primes, so its topic is 'on primes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject or topic, here the puzzle's own subject of prime numbers.

clue.text: Nameless type of paint, the first to mark wood

indicators.note: the word for a name is removed from the paint

parts.note: enamel is a glossy paint

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A decorator marks wood with a nameless type of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing NAME from ENAMEL leaves EL.
explanation.definitionFit: The timber of a tall deciduous tree, so a kind of wood.

clue.text: Preach new realism about love

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the circle
the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A preacher of a new realism about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges REALISM into MRALISE, which goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture others on right and wrong, as a sermon does.

clue.text: Proposal from cockney woman

parts.note: off can mean from, as in take it off me
her with the h dropped, as a cockney says it

explanation.surface: A proposal of marriage from a London woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, are said to drop their h's.
explanation.definitionFit: A bid or proposition put forward for acceptance.

clue.text: Sawn-off gun raised: it is held by prime suspect on run

indicators.note: the pieces are held inside the number

parts.note: five is a prime number

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upward
the end of the weapon is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before cutting

explanation.surface: A sawn-off shotgun is held up by the prime suspect on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime suspect' looks like one phrase, but 'prime' gives the number and 'suspect on run' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fleeing the police is an escapee, a suspect at large.

clue.text: So, prime suspect is to swear oath?

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective, unreliable, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: So, the prime suspect must take an oath in court?
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge one's word, like an oath, is to vow something solemnly.

clue.text: Betrays no hiding place for anything less than a pound

indicators.note: the hiding place is denied a part in the word

parts.note: denounces means informs against
a den is a lair or hideout

explanation.surface: An informer betrays an associate who has nowhere to hide for under a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: In imperial weights there are sixteen of them in a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of weight, sixteen to the pound, so any weight under a pound is some of them.

clue.text: Prime and irrational number? Large primes can't be this

parts.note: e, the base of natural logarithms, is irrational
apart from two, no prime is divisible by two

explanation.surface: A mathematical puzzle about prime and irrational numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' does double duty: it gives L and qualifies the primes, since only the small prime two is even, a looseness the setter admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Divisible only by itself and one, so a prime number.

clue.text: Go back to EU, generally friendless in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the run of letters is read back to front
the word generally loses its friend, ALLY, so only the letters before it are used

explanation.surface: A Brexit politician, generally friendless, retreating back to the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friendless' strips ALLY from 'generally', leaving GENER; with EU that is EUGENER, which 'in retreat' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back on a promise or deal, a variant spelling of renege.

clue.text: They could kill & maim, say

parts.note: an ampersand as in rock 'n' roll

indicators.note: say here means 'as one might pronounce it', so the injury word is heard in a dropped-r accent rather than spelt

parts.note: to maim is to injure badly

explanation.surface: A warning about people who could kill and maim.
explanation.walkthrough: '&' is 'n' and 'maim, say' is INJURE pronounced in a non-rhotic accent, INJA.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese martial artists trained as assassins and spies.

clue.text: Prime number — up to zero

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upward

parts.note: two is the smallest prime

explanation.surface: A prime number is counted up to zero.
explanation.walkthrough: A dialect word from the north of England for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word from northern England meaning nothing at all.

clue.text: Teach two nurses to take on part of the crossword

indicators.note: the nurses take the crossword piece on board, holding it

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse, so two of them
a light is one of a crossword's answers

explanation.surface: Two nurses take on part of a crossword to teach each other.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'light' is the crossword term for an entry in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct someone and so give them knowledge or understanding.

clue.text: Heartless visitor delivers blow

indicators.note: the central letter is removed

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A heartless visitor delivers a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden blast of wind, as the wind blows.

clue.text: Zero is new factor for all primes

parts.note: every prime is divisible by one and itself

explanation.surface: A mathematical statement that zero is a new factor of all primes.
explanation.definitionFit: Not any, not a single one, so a count of zero.

clue.text: Perhaps using skis, with the French slopes around them

indicators.note: the leaning word wraps around the article

parts.note: heels means leans or tilts, as a ship does
les is French for the, plural

explanation.surface: A skier on French slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slopes' is a verb, tilts, not ski runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge or skis move without any wheels, so skiing is one example.

clue.text: Prime made out to include another

indicators.note: the first word includes the second inside it

parts.note: seen means made out, discerned
another prime, five, the Roman V

explanation.surface: A prime number made out to include another.
explanation.definitionFit: Divisible only by itself and one, so a prime number.
